builder: Hughes Aircraft Company / NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)

lunar_landing_coordinates.feature: Surveyor Crater (inside southeastern inner slope, ~10 to 14 deg incline)

physical_dimensions.structure: Triangular space frame constructed of thin-wall 7075-T6 tubular aluminum alloy

mast_assembly.solar_panel: Single planar array of 3,960 solar cells (~1.0m x 0.7m), supplying up to 89W electrical power
mast_assembly.high_gain_planar_antenna: Gimballed flat rectangular planar array antenna (~0.80m x 0.50m) for TV downlink

landing_gear.configuration: 120-degree radial spacing, hinged tubular inverted tripod struts
landing_gear.shock_absorbers: Hydraulic dashpot and crushable aluminum honeycomb footpads

television_system.vidicon_camera: Focal length 25-100mm zoom lens, mounted vertically with 360-degree azimuth and elevation mirror turret

soil_mechanics_surface_sampler.mechanism: Articulated pantograph / scissor arm driven by electric motors
soil_mechanics_surface_sampler.bearing_strength_tests_performed: Multiple bearing and impact penetrations confirming soil bearing capacity of 1.8 to 5.5 N/cm^2

propulsion.vernier_engines: 3 liquid engines burning monomethylhydrazine (MMH) and MON-10 oxidizer, throttleable 130 to 460 N thrust each

apollo_12_rendezvous.time_on_moon_prior_to_visit: 31 months (974 days) exposed to vacuum, solar radiation, thermal cycling (-180C to +120C), and micrometeoroid flux
hardware_retrieved_by_astronauts: Television Camera Unit (including vidicon tube, optics, filter wheel, and electronics housing)
Surface Sampler Scoop bucket and section of articulated arm
Sections of unpainted 7075-T6 aluminum tubing from landing leg 3 strut
Sections of electrical cabling with Kapton/Teflon insulation

post_flight_findings.streptococcus_mitis_claim: Microbiological testing initially claimed 50-100 viable bacteria inside camera foam, later determined to be laboratory contamination during sterile bench inspection in Houston
post_flight_findings.optical_degradation: Severe browning and pitting of optical mirrors and white thermal paint due to solar UV radiation and sandblasting from Intrepid descent engine exhaust
post_flight_findings.micrometeoroid_flux: Counted microscopic pits proving lunar surface bombardment rate was lower than pre-Apollo conservative estimates
